correctness.rationale: The two-state semigroup gives off-diagonals u and v and output probability z=u+(1-u-v)q. The entropy chain rule and conditional variance decomposition prove the objective and its strict concavity; positivity of the channel gives an interior optimizer. The gradient of the homogeneous conditional entropy in positive input weights is the vector of point-mass mismatch costs, and the point-mass maximum and KL data processing give the minimax equality. In the fixed gap regime, at q=c/L the term h'(q)−h'(z) is asymptotic to atL/c, the extra factor (1−k)h'(z) is O(t log L), and h(v)−h(u) contributes −ΔtL. Thus concavity brackets q* at a/(ΔL). On that bracket the entropy Taylor error is O(t²/q)=o(t). The term −Δq*log(1/t) cancels the constant +a, while −a log(1/q*) converts a log(1/t)−a log a to a(L−log L). At equal rates the symmetric optimizer is exactly 1/2. In the varying-rate family the compact-interior first-order objective and derivative limits give the stated g_η; its strictly negative second derivative and derivative sign brackets localize the finite-time maximizer away from either endpoint before evaluating the value. The large-η slope equation has leading term κ/Q_η, as claimed. The varying-rate expansion is pointwise at fixed κ>0, η≥0, not uniform near a moving boundary. Inspected but did not execute verification/minimax_verifier.py; its recorded 76 checks are finite diagnostics, not the proof.

value.rationale: The maximization is singular at fixed asymmetry and regular at symmetry. The optimizer scale and the negative log-log term quantify the singularity, and the varying-rate theorem identifies the transition window in which neither fixed-rate formula can be used uniformly. Resolving the order-t value and the optimizer in that window is useful beyond recomputing a binary-channel leading coefficient.
